cards.front: What is an ecotone? Give examples.
cards.back: A transition zone between two ecosystems with characteristics of both, often showing higher species diversity (edge effect). Examples: mangroves (land-sea), estuaries, grassland-forest fringe.

cards.front: What are the criteria for a Biodiversity Hotspot, and which hotspots cover India?
cards.back: ≥1,500 endemic vascular plants AND ≥70% habitat loss. India: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

cards.front: Differentiate: Kyoto Protocol vs Paris Agreement.
cards.back: Kyoto (1997): binding targets only for developed (Annex-I) countries, top-down. Paris (2015): all countries submit NDCs, bottom-up, goal to keep warming well below 2°C (pursue 1.5°C), 5-yearly global stocktake.

cards.front: Difference between National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary and Biosphere Reserve?
cards.back: NP: strict protection, no human activity, species+habitat focus. WLS: certain activities (grazing) may be allowed. BR (UNESCO MAB): large areas with core, buffer, transition zones including human communities.

cards.front: Which Act is called the 'umbrella legislation' for environment in India and why?
cards.back: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — enacted after Bhopal; empowers the Centre to take all measures to protect environment, set standards, and frame rules (EIA, CRZ notifications flow from it).

cards.front: What is eutrophication and its consequence?
cards.back: Nutrient (N, P) enrichment of water bodies → algal blooms → decomposition depletes dissolved oxygen (hypoxia) → fish kills, dead zones. Cultural eutrophication is human-induced (fertiliser runoff, sewage).

cards.front: What do the IUCN Red List categories CR, EN, VU mean? Give an Indian CR species.
cards.back: Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable — decreasing threat order. Indian CR examples: Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Bengal Florican.

cards.front: What is Carbon Sequestration? Name two natural sinks.
cards.back: Long-term capture and storage of atmospheric CO2. Natural sinks: oceans (largest), forests, soils, mangroves ('blue carbon'). Artificial: CCS/CCUS technologies.

cards.front: What is Project Tiger and under which body is it implemented?
cards.back: Launched 1973 (9 reserves) for in-situ tiger conservation; now 50+ reserves under the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2006.

cards.front: What is the composition and jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
cards.back: Established under NGT Act, 2010; Chairperson (retired SC judge) + judicial & expert members. Handles civil environmental cases (7 laws incl. EPA, Water, Air, Forest Conservation Acts) — but NOT the Wildlife Protection Act.
